questions.question_english: Before a competent authority agrees to write off a loss caused by the negligence of a government servant, what is the prerequisite requirement?
options_english: The concerned government servant must be permanently transferred to a distant non-sensitive administrative post.
The concerned government servant must give written consent authorizing the administration to write off the loss.
All avenues to recover the amount from the responsible servant must be exhausted.
The statutory audit department team must physically inspect and audit the government servant's private residence.
questions.explanation_english: Under Rule 37 of GFR 2017 and general principles of government financial propriety, public money cannot be written off to shield or absolve an employee whose negligence or misconduct resulted in government loss. Before a competent authority can sanction a write-off, the administration must demonstrate that formal disciplinary proceedings under the CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965 were initiated, personal responsibility was fixed, and all legal and administrative avenues to recover the loss from the responsible official (including deduction from salary, adjustment against pensionary benefits/gratuity, or legal decree) have been thoroughly pursued and completely exhausted. Writing off is an extraordinary measure of last resort, permissible only when recovery is definitively established to be impossible.
questions.explanation_hindi: जीएफआर 2017 के नियम 37 तथा वित्तीय औचित्य के सिद्धांतों के अनुसार, किसी कर्मचारी की लापरवाही या कदाचार से हुई सरकारी हानि को केवल प्रशासनिक सुविधा के लिए बट्टे खाते में नहीं डाला जा सकता। सक्षम प्राधिकारी द्वारा बट्टे खाते में डालने की मंजूरी देने से पूर्व यह सुनिश्चित करना अनिवार्य है कि संबंधित कर्मचारी के विरुद्ध सीसीएस (सीसीए) नियमों के तहत अनुशासनात्मक कार्रवाई की गई हो, उसकी व्यक्तिगत जिम्मेदारी तय की गई हो, तथा उससे वेतन कटौती, ग्रेच्युटी/पेंशन समायोजन या विधिक कार्रवाई के माध्यम से वसूली के समस्त रास्ते पूरी तरह समाप्त (exhaust) हो चुके हों। बट्टे खाते में डालना केवल उसी समय अंतिम उपाय के रूप में स्वीकृत किया जा सकता है जब वसूली पूर्णतः असंभव हो।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (c) All avenues to recover the amount from the responsible servant must be exhausted.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: responsible servant must be exhausted. Before a competent authority can write off a public financial loss caused by employee negligence, all reasonable administrative and legal avenues to recover the loss from the responsible official must be fully exhausted. Writing off public funds occurs only when recovery efforts prove completely impossible despite formal disciplinary or recovery actions.

questions.question_english:
Consider the following statements regarding the Delegation of Financial Powers Rules (DFPR):
I. Powers are delegated subject to the availability of sanctioned budget provisions.
II. A delegated authority can further sub-delegate its financial powers to any lower authority at its own discretion without formal regulatory approval.
III. Delegated powers must be exercised in strict accordance with the general financial principles and cannons of financial propriety.
IV. Sanctioning of expenditure is strictly limited to the quantum and ceiling of power delegated.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
options_english: I, II and III
I, III and IV
II, III and IV
I, II, III and IV
questions.explanation_english:
Under the Delegation of Financial Powers Rules (DFPR) and GFR 2017:
1. Statement I is correct: Rule 3 of DFPR explicitly states that all financial powers delegated to any authority are subject to the condition that funds are available under the relevant sanctioned budget head.
2. Statement II is incorrect: Under the legal principle 'delegatus non potest delegare' and DFPR provisions, a subordinate authority to whom financial power is delegated cannot further sub-delegate that power to another lower authority at its own discretion unless expressly empowered to do so by general or special orders of the delegating competent authority.
3. Statement III is correct: All delegated authorities must exercise their powers with due regard to the Cannons of Financial Propriety (GFR Rule 21) and statutory accounting rules.
4. Statement IV is correct: The power to incur expenditure or issue sanctions cannot exceed the specific financial ceiling or scope delegated to that post.
Therefore, Statements I, III, and IV are correct.
questions.explanation_hindi:
वित्तीय शक्ति प्रत्यायोजन नियमावली (DFPR) और GFR 2017 के अनुसार:
1. कथन I सही है: DFPR के नियम 3 में स्पष्ट उल्लेख है कि प्रत्यायोजित शक्तियों का प्रयोग संबंधित बजट शीर्ष में पर्याप्त निधि की उपलब्धता के अधीन ही किया जा सकता है। बिना बजट कोई व्यय स्वीकृत नहीं हो सकता।
2. कथन II गलत है: प्रशासनिक विधि के मान्य सिद्धांत ('delegatus non potest delegare') के अनुसार, जिस प्राधिकारी को शक्तियां प्रत्यायोजित की गई हैं, वह सक्षम प्राधिकारी के स्पष्ट आदेशों या नियमों के बिना अपने स्वविवेक से उन शक्तियों को किसी अन्य अधीनस्थ प्राधिकारी को उप-प्रत्यायोजित नहीं कर सकता।
3. कथन III सही है: वित्तीय शक्तियों का प्रयोग वित्तीय औचित्य के सिद्धांतों (GFR नियम 21) और स्थापित वित्तीय नियमों के अनुसार ही किया जाना अनिवार्य है।
4. कथन IV सही है: व्यय की स्वीकृति प्रत्यायोजित मौद्रिक सीमा और अधिकार क्षेत्र के भीतर ही दी जा सकती है।
अतः कथन I, III और IV सही हैं (विकल्प B सही है)।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) I, III and IV

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Delegated financial powers must be exercised strictly within approved budget allocations, monetary limits, and general financial principles. An authority delegated financial power cannot sub-delegate those powers to lower officials at personal discretion without explicit regulatory authorization or formal approval from higher competent authorities under delegation rules.

questions.question_english: Who holds the ultimate inherent power to write off any loss of public money or stores, beyond the powers delegated to subordinate authorities under DFPR?
options_english: The Head of Office acting in consultation with the local Pay and Accounts Office.
The respective administrative Ministry/Department with the concurrence of the Ministry of Finance.
The Comptroller and Auditor General of India exercising constitutional powers.
The Governor of the Reserve Bank of India in consultation with central banks.
questions.explanation_english: Under Rule 37 of GFR 2017 and Rule 13 of the Delegation of Financial Powers Rules (DFPR), 1978, the sovereign and ultimate financial power to sanction the write-off of public money, stores, or revenue losses vests in the Central Government. Where the monetary value of a loss exceeds the specific delegated financial ceilings of Heads of Offices, Heads of Departments, or administrative Ministries, the write-off can only be sanctioned by the administrative Ministry/Department with the mandatory concurrence of the Ministry of Finance (Department of Expenditure). The CAG is an external constitutional auditor and does not possess executive power to write off losses, nor do the RBI or local PAOs hold such authority.
questions.explanation_hindi: जीएफआर 2017 के नियम 37 तथा वित्तीय शक्तियों के प्रत्यायोजन नियम (DFPR), 1978 के नियम 13 के अनुसार, सार्वजनिक धन, भंडार अथवा राजस्व की हानि को बट्टे खाते में डालने की अंतिम और संप्रभु वित्तीय शक्ति केंद्र सरकार में निहित है। यदि हानि की राशि कार्यालय प्रमुखों, विभागाध्यक्षों अथवा मंत्रालयों को प्रत्यायोजित वित्तीय सीमा से अधिक हो जाती है, तो बट्टे खाते में डालने की स्वीकृति संबंधित प्रशासनिक मंत्रालय/विभाग द्वारा वित्त मंत्रालय (व्यय विभाग) की अनिवार्य सहमति प्राप्त करके ही जारी की जा सकती है। कैग (CAG) केवल बाह्य सांविधिक लेखापरीक्षक है और उसके पास बट्टे खाते में डालने की कार्यकारी शक्ति नहीं होती, न ही आरबीआई या स्थानीय पीएओ के पास ऐसा अधिकार होता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (b) The respective Ministry/Department with concurrence of Ministry of Finance.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: concurrence of Ministry of Finance. When financial losses or store write-offs exceed monetary limits delegated to subordinate officials, ultimate authority rests with the administrative Ministry or Department. Exercising these higher powers requires formal concurrence from the Ministry of Finance, ensuring centralized fiscal oversight over major write-offs across all executive government branches.

questions.question_english: Under the Delegation of Financial Powers Rules (DFPR) and General Financial Rules (GFR), what is the primary role of the Integrated Financial Adviser (IFA / FA) attached to a Ministry or Department?
options_english: To act as the primary drawing and disbursing officer for processing monthly salary disbursements across the Ministry.
To physically disburse cash payments and petty allowances to all registered commercial vendors and contractors.
To write and evaluate the Annual Confidential Performance Appraisal Reports of all teaching staff in the state.
To provide financial scrutiny, concurrence, and advice to the Secretary and competent administrative authorities before they exercise delegated financial powers.
questions.explanation_english: Under the Scheme of Integrated Financial Adviser (IFA) outlined in GFR and DFPR, the Financial Adviser (FA) is integrated with the administrative Ministry to assist the Secretary (who is the Chief Accounting Authority) in budget formulation, expenditure control, scheme evaluation, and financial decision-making. The primary role of the FA is to provide expert financial advice, ensure observance of financial propriety and GFR rules, and accord financial concurrence before the competent administrative authority exercises financial powers on proposals beyond delegated powers of lower officers or requiring IFA consultation. The FA does not perform cash disbursement or routine DDO clerical duties, but acts as the internal financial conscience and fiscal guardian of the Ministry.
questions.explanation_hindi: जीएफआर और DFPR के तहत एकीकृत वित्तीय सलाहकार (IFA) योजना के अनुसार, वित्तीय सलाहकार (FA) प्रशासनिक मंत्रालय के सचिव (जो मुख्य लेखा प्राधिकारी होते हैं) को बजट निर्माण, व्यय नियंत्रण, योजनाओं के मूल्यांकन और वित्तीय निर्णय लेने में सहायता प्रदान करता है। FA की प्राथमिक भूमिका वित्तीय नियमों की संवीक्षा करना, वित्तीय औचित्य और GFR के नियमों का पालन सुनिश्चित करना तथा सक्षम प्रशासनिक प्राधिकारी द्वारा शक्तियों का प्रयोग करने से पूर्व वित्तीय सहमति (concurrence) और सलाह देना है। FA का कार्य नियमित नकद संवितरण या DDO का कार्य करना नहीं है, बल्कि मंत्रालय में वित्तीय अनुशासन और राजकोषीय नियंत्रण बनाए रखना है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) To provide financial concurrence and advice before competent authority exercises delegated powers.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: before competent authority exercises delegated powers. The Financial Adviser attached to a Ministry or Department provides financial scrutiny, advice, and concurrence before competent administrative authorities exercise delegated financial powers. The Financial Adviser evaluates expenditure proposals for propriety, rule compliance, and budget availability, assisting administrative heads in maintaining overall fiscal discipline and effective budget management.

questions.question_english: After executing electronic payments to various contractors and vendors via the PFMS portal, what critical and mandatory accounting procedure must the Drawing and Disbursing Officer (DDO) / Principal promptly undertake?
options_english: Purging all transaction logs and electronic audit trails from local office workstations to conserve hard disk storage.
Returning the supplied materials and equipment to the vendor to obtain duplicate physical cash receipts.
Undertaking prompt accounting reconciliation of electronic payment disbursements with the Cash Book entries and the daily Bank Scroll.
Attesting and printing every digital payment confirmation receipt on non-judicial stamp paper for institutional filing.
questions.explanation_english: Under Rule 53 and Rule 86 of GFR 2017, read in conjunction with the Central Government Account (Receipts and Payments) Rules, the execution of electronic payments through PFMS does not conclude the accounting process. The Drawing and Disbursing Officer (DDO) / Principal is statutorily responsible for carrying out prompt and systematic reconciliation of the payments. Specifically, the DDO must verify the Electronic Payment Advice (EPA) generated by PFMS, record the disbursements accurately in the Cash Book, and reconcile the Cash Book entries against the daily Bank Scroll received from the paying bank branch. Reconciliation confirms that the intended payee's account was credited successfully, guards against duplicate debits or unauthorized withdrawals, and ensures that failed/returned transactions are promptly re-credited in the official accounts. Hence, option C is correct.

questions.question_english: What is the meaning and purpose of a "Permanent Advance" or "Imprest" in the context of government offices and schools?
options_english: A fixed sum placed at the disposal of an officer to meet urgent and petty contingent expenditures before funds can be drawn on regular bills.
A permanent administrative increment granted in the basic pay scale of a government employee.
A long-term interest-bearing loan sanctioned to an employee for constructing a permanent residential house.

questions.explanation_english:
Under Rule 322 of General Financial Rules (GFR), 2017 and Central Government Account (Receipts and Payments) Rules:
1. Definition: A permanent advance, universally termed an "Imprest", is a fixed sum of money placed at the disposal of an administrative officer (such as a Head of Office, Drawing and Disbursing Officer, or School Principal) to enable immediate payment for routine, small-value contingent office expenses before funds can be drawn on regular contingent bills from the Pay and Accounts Office (PAO).
2. Administrative Utility: In the day-to-day administration of an office or educational institution, numerous small expenses arise (e.g., postage, urgent minor repairs, cartage, emergency stationery). Presenting individual bills to the PAO for each petty transaction would cause severe delays and operational paralysis. The imprest system provides the operational flexibility needed to settle petty charges immediately.
3. Continuous Replenishment: As petty payments are made from the imprest, paid vouchers are accumulated and submitted via an imprest recoupment bill to reimburse and restore the cash balance to its original sanctioned limit.
Therefore, Option A correctly defines an imprest.
questions.explanation_hindi:
सामान्य वित्तीय नियम (GFR) 2017 के नियम 322 और केंद्रीय सरकारी लेखा (प्राप्ति और भुगतान) नियमों के अनुसार:
1. परिभाषा: स्थायी अग्रिम, जिसे सामान्यतः "इम्प्रेस्ट" (Imprest) कहा जाता है, किसी प्रशासनिक अधिकारी (जैसे कार्यालय प्रमुख, आहरण एवं संवितरण अधिकारी / DDO या विद्यालय प्राचार्य) के अधीन रखी गई धन की एक निश्चित राशि होती है, ताकि वेतन एवं लेखा कार्यालय (PAO) से नियमित आकस्मिक बिलों पर धन प्राप्त होने की प्रतीक्षा किए बिना दिन-प्रतिदिन के छोटे-मोटे आकस्मिक खर्चों का तत्काल भुगतान किया जा सके।
2. प्रशासनिक उपयोगिता: किसी कार्यालय या शिक्षण संस्थान के दैनिक प्रशासन में कई छोटे खर्च सामने आते हैं (जैसे डाक खर्च, छोटी आकस्मिक मरम्मत, स्थानीय ढुलाई, तात्कालिक स्टेशनरी आदि)। प्रत्येक छोटे लेनदेन के लिए पीएओ में अलग-अलग बिल भेजना भारी देरी और प्रशासनिक कार्यों में बाधा उत्पन्न करेगा। इम्प्रेस्ट प्रणाली इन छोटे भुगतानों को तुरंत निपटाने की सुविधा प्रदान करती है।
3. निरंतर प्रतिपूर्ति: इम्प्रेस्ट से भुगतान किए जाने के बाद, भुगतान किए गए वाउचरों को एकत्र कर एक प्रतिपूर्ति बिल (Recoupment Bill) के माध्यम से प्रस्तुत किया जाता है जिससे नकद शेष राशि वापस मूल स्वीकृत सीमा तक पहुँच जाती है।
अतः विकल्प A सही परिभाषा प्रस्तुत करता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) A fixed sum placed at disposal of an officer to meet petty contingent expenditure.

questions.question_english: A school Principal has delegated financial power to sanction contingent expenditure up to Rs. 20,000 per occasion. To expedite the work without seeking sanction from the higher authority, the Principal issues three separate sanction orders of Rs. 15,000 each on the same day for the same work. Is this administrative action justified?
options_english: No, splitting demand or expenditure to avoid obtaining the sanction of a higher competent authority is strictly prohibited under financial rules.

questions.explanation_english: Under Rule 157 of GFR 2017 and standard provisions of DFPR, a demand for goods, services, or execution of works shall not be divided or split into small quantities or multiple sanctions merely to evade the necessity of obtaining the sanction of higher authority required with reference to the estimated value of the total demand. Here, the estimated cost of the plumbing work is Rs. 45,000, which exceeds the Principal's delegated ceiling of Rs. 20,000. Splitting this single requirement into three sanctions of Rs. 15,000 each on the same day constitutes an intentional circumvention of financial rules and is an irregularity liable to audit objection and disciplinary action under Central Civil Services (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules.
questions.explanation_hindi: जीएफआर 2017 के नियम 157 और DFPR के सुस्थापित प्रावधानों के अनुसार, कुल मांग के अनुमानित मूल्य के संदर्भ में अपेक्षित उच्च प्राधिकारी की स्वीकृति प्राप्त करने की आवश्यकता से बचने के लिए मांग, सेवाओं या कार्यों को छोटे टुकड़ों या एकाधिक स्वीकृतियों में विभाजित (splitting of sanction) नहीं किया जाएगा। प्रस्तुत मामले में, प्लंबिंग कार्य का कुल अनुमानित व्यय 45,000 रुपये है, जो प्राचार्य की 20,000 रुपये की प्रत्यायोजित वित्तीय सीमा से अधिक है। एक ही दिन एक ही कार्य के लिए 15,000 रुपये की तीन अलग-अलग स्वीकृतियां जारी करना वित्तीय नियमों का गंभीर उल्लंघन और वित्तीय अनियमितता है, जिस पर लेखापरीक्षा आपत्ति और अनुशासनात्मक कार्रवाई की जा सकती है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) No, splitting demand to avoid obtaining sanction of higher authority is prohibited.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: sanction of higher authority is prohibited. Issuing multiple smaller financial sanctions on the same day for a single work requirement to bypass monetary limits assigned to higher competent authorities is strictly prohibited. Splitting financial demands violates delegation rules. Procuring officers must seek formal sanction from the higher authority holding appropriate monetary sanctioning powers for the total project cost.

III. सत्यापन उस स्टोर-कीपर द्वारा ही किया जाना चाहिए जो रजिस्टर का रखरखाव करता है।
उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-से सही हैं?
options_hindi: केवल I और II
केवल II और III

questions.question_english:
Consider the following statements regarding the physical verification of stores under GFR 2017:
I. The verification must be carried out in the presence of the officer or custodian responsible for the physical custody of the stores.
II. Discrepancies, shortages, or damages detected during verification must be brought to the notice of the competent authority immediately.
III. The verification should ideally be conducted by the storekeeper who maintains the stock registers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
options_english: I and II only
II and III only
I and III only
I, II and III
questions.explanation_english:
Under Rule 213 of GFR 2017:
- Statement I is correct: Physical verification must be conducted in the presence of the officer responsible for the custody of the stores or their authorized nominee, so that any physical movement or query can be clarified on the spot.
- Statement II is correct: Rule 213(3) explicitly mandates that shortages, damages, unserviceable items, or surplus inventory revealed during physical verification must be promptly brought to the notice of the competent authority for investigation and necessary adjustment.
- Statement III is incorrect: Rule 213(2) strictly dictates that the verification must NEVER be conducted by a person who is the storekeeper, who has physical custody of the stores, or who is directly subordinate to the storekeeper. An independent officer or committee must be entrusted with verification to prevent bias, concealment, and conflict of interest.
Hence, statements I and II are correct, making (A) the correct choice.
questions.explanation_hindi:
सामान्य वित्तीय नियम (GFR), 2017 के नियम 213 के अनुसार:
- कथन I सही है: भंडारों का भौतिक सत्यापन सदैव उस अधिकारी या कर्मचारी की उपस्थिति में किया जाना चाहिए जो उन भंडारों की वास्तविक अभिरक्षा (Custody) के लिए जिम्मेदार है।
- कथन II सही है: नियम 213(3) के अनुसार सत्यापन के दौरान यदि कोई कमी (Shortage), क्षति (Damage) या अन्य विसंगतियां पाई जाती हैं, तो उन्हें बिना किसी विलंब के सक्षम प्राधिकारी के संज्ञान में लाया जाना अनिवार्य है ताकि जवाबदेही तय की जा सके।
- कथन III गलत है: नियम 213(2) में स्पष्ट प्रावधान है कि भौतिक सत्यापन कभी भी उस स्टोर-कीपर या उसके सीधे अधीनस्थ कर्मचारी द्वारा नहीं किया जाएगा जिसके पास भंडारों की अभिरक्षा या रिकॉर्ड रखने का प्रभार है। निष्पक्षता सुनिश्चित करने के लिए यह कार्य किसी स्वतंत्र अधिकारी या समिति द्वारा ही किया जाना चाहिए।
अतः केवल कथन I और II सही हैं।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) I and II

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Physical verification of stores must be conducted in the presence of the store custodian, and any detected shortages, damages, or discrepancies must be immediately reported to competent authorities. To ensure objective verification, the inspection must be conducted by an independent officer or committee, never by the storekeeper responsible for stock custody.

questions.question_english: A school Principal urgently requires 10 whiteboards for newly constructed classrooms, with a total estimated cost of Rs. 35,000. Under the provisions of GFR 2017, how should the Principal proceed to procure these whiteboards through GeM?
options_english: By comparing prices of at least three different GeM manufacturers and selecting the L1 bidder
By directly selecting any random registered seller offering whiteboards on the portal
By calling a physical open tender outside GeM since the purchase amount exceeds Rs. 25,000
By purchasing the required items from the local market directly without verifying GeM availability
questions.explanation_english: According to Rule 149(ii) of GFR 2017, for procurement of goods valued between Rs. 25,000 and Rs. 5,00,000 on the Government e-Marketplace (GeM), the purchasing authority (Head of Office / Principal / DDO) must mandate an online comparison of products from at least three different manufacturers available on the portal. The buyer must verify that the products meet the required technical specifications, warranty, and delivery schedule, and then award the purchase order to the lowest-priced (L1) qualified bidder. Because the estimated procurement value of the whiteboards is Rs. 35,000, it falls within the Rs. 25,000 to Rs. 5,00,000 threshold. The Principal cannot bypass this comparison to make a direct single-seller purchase (permitted only up to Rs. 25,000), nor bypass GeM to purchase locally without a Non-Availability Certificate.
questions.explanation_hindi: GFR 2017 के नियम 149(ii) के अनुसार, गवर्नमेंट ई-मार्केटप्लेस (GeM) पर ₹25,000 से अधिक और ₹5,00,000 तक की वस्तुओं की खरीद के लिए, क्रय प्राधिकारी (कार्यालय प्रमुख / विद्यालय प्राचार्य / DDO) को पोर्टल पर उपलब्ध कम से कम तीन अलग-अलग निर्माताओं के उत्पादों के विनिर्देशों और मूल्यों की ऑनलाइन तुलना करना अनिवार्य है। इसके उपरांत निर्धारित तकनीकी विनिर्देशों को पूरा करने वाले न्यूनतम मूल्य बोलीदाता (L1) को खरीद आदेश जारी किया जाना चाहिए। चूंकि 10 व्हाइटबोर्ड की अनुमानित लागत ₹35,000 है, यह ₹25,000 से ₹5,00,000 की श्रेणी में आती है। प्राचार्य किसी एक विक्रेता से सीधे खरीद नहीं कर सकते (सीधी खरीद केवल ₹25,000 तक मान्य है), और न ही GeM को नजरअंदाज करके खुले बाजार या बाहरी खुली निविदा का सहारा ले सकते हैं।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) By comparing prices of at least three different GeM manufacturers and selecting L1 bidder.

The purchasing authority is required to evaluate options based on required technical specifications and select the lowest cost (L1) offer among qualified sellers.

questions.question_english:
Consider the following statements regarding the applicability and scope of the General Financial Rules (GFR), 2017:
I. The rules are deemed applicable to Autonomous Bodies except to the extent that their own specific rules have been approved by the Government.
II. GFR 2017 completely supersedes all previous editions of the General Financial Rules.
III. State Governments are statutorily bound to adopt GFR 2017 without any modification.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
options_english: I and II only
II and III only
I and III only
I, II and III
questions.explanation_english: Statement I is correct: Rule 1 of GFR 2017 provides that these rules are deemed applicable to Autonomous Bodies except to the extent that separate financial rules have been framed by them with the approval of the Central Government. Statement II is correct: GFR 2017 supersedes GFR 2005 and all earlier editions. Statement III is incorrect: Under the federal constitutional structure (Articles 282 and 283), State Governments operate under their own State Financial Codes and rules enacted by state legislatures; they are not legally bound to adopt the Central Government's GFR 2017, although they may draw inspiration from it.
questions.explanation_hindi: कथन I सही है: GFR 2017 के नियम 1 के अनुसार, ये नियम केंद्र सरकार के स्वायत्त निकायों पर भी लागू माने जाते हैं, बशर्ते उन निकायों ने सरकार के अनुमोदन से अपने अलग नियम न बनाए हों। कथन II सही है: GFR 2017 ने पूर्ववर्ती GFR 2005 और सभी पुराने संस्करणों को पूरी तरह से प्रतिस्थापित (supersede) कर दिया है। कथन III गलत है: भारत के संघीय ढांचे (अनुच्छेद 282 और 283) के तहत राज्य सरकारों की अपनी वित्तीय नियमावलियां (State Financial Rules/Codes) होती हैं; राज्य सरकारें केंद्र के GFR 2017 को बिना संशोधन अपनाने के लिए कानूनी रूप से बाध्य नहीं हैं। अतः केवल I और II सही हैं।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) I and II

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: The General Financial Rules 2017 automatically apply to autonomous bodies unless those organizations have framed their own specific financial rules approved by the Central Government. Furthermore, the 2017 framework completely replaced and superseded all pre- existing versions of financial rules. However, state governments operate under their own autonomous constitutional powers and financial guidelines, meaning central financial rules are not mandatory for them.

questions.question_english: Which centralized online portal has been established by the Government of India (administered by the Controller General of Accounts) for the electronic collection and remittance of non-tax revenues and user fees, as mandated under GFR provisions?
options_english: Bharat BillPay Unified Collection Platform
Government e-Marketplace (GeM) Transaction Hub
NITI Aayog Public Policy and Development Portal
Non-Tax Receipt Portal (NTRP) / Bharatkosh
questions.explanation_english: Bharatkosh, formally known as the Non-Tax Receipt Portal (NTRP - bharatkosh.gov.in), is the flagship digital initiative developed and managed by the Controller General of Accounts (CGA), Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance. It serves as a unified, one-stop payment gateway for citizens, corporations, and institutions to remit all non-tax government dues—such as user fees, license fees, RTI fees, examination application fees, fines, and departmental receipts—directly into the Consolidated Fund of India. Under GFR 2017 (Rule 48), ministries and departments are mandated to integrate their billing and collection systems with Bharatkosh to eliminate manual cash and physical drafts, ensuring transparent, real-time accounting and reconciliation. Hence, option D is correct.
questions.explanation_hindi: भारतकोश (Bharatkosh), जिसे औपचारिक रूप से गैर-कर रसीद पोर्टल (Non-Tax Receipt Portal - NTRP) के रूप में जाना जाता है, वित्त मंत्रालय के व्यय विभाग के तहत महालेखा नियंत्रक (CGA) द्वारा विकसित और संचालित एक केंद्रीय वेब पोर्टल है। यह नागरिकों, संस्थाओं और निगमों को सभी प्रकार के गैर-कर सरकारी राजस्व—जैसे कि परीक्षा शुल्क, आरटीआई शुल्क, उपयोगकर्ता प्रभार, लाइसेंस शुल्क, जुर्माने आदि—को सीधे भारत की संचित निधि (Consolidated Fund of India) में 24x7 ऑनलाइन जमा करने की सुविधा प्रदान करता है। GFR 2017 के नियम 48 के तहत सभी मंत्रालयों और संबद्ध कार्यालयों से अपेक्षा की जाती है कि वे नकद अथवा डीडी संग्रह के स्थान पर भारतकोश पोर्टल का उपयोग सुनिश्चित करें ताकि त्वरित व पारदर्शी लेखांकन हो सके। अतः विकल्प D सही उत्तर है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) Non-Tax Receipt Portal (NTRP) / Bharatkosh

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Bharatkosh Bharatkosh, also known as the Non-Tax Receipt Portal, is the centralized online portal developed by the Controller General of Accounts to facilitate online collection of non-tax revenues, user fees, and statutory receipts. Public departments are required to utilize Bharatkosh to enable citizens and entities to deposit government dues digitally.

questions.question_hindi: एक विद्यालय के प्राचार्य को परीक्षा एवं मुद्रण सामग्री की आपूर्ति के लिए एक विक्रेता के 40,000 रुपये के स्वीकृत बिल का भुगतान करना है। विक्रेता बैंकिंग औपचारिकताओं से बचने के लिए नकद (Cash) भुगतान का अनुरोध करता है। GFR 2017 और सरकारी कोषागार नियमों के अंतर्गत प्राचार्य को क्या करना चाहिए?
options_hindi: विद्यालय के काउंटर पर एकत्र दैनिक विद्यार्थी विकास शुल्क/जुर्माने की नकद राशि से विक्रेता को सीधे नकद भुगतान कर देना चाहिए।
अपने व्यक्तिगत मोबाइल UPI ऐप से पूरी राशि का भुगतान कर देना चाहिए और बाद में कार्यालय से इसकी औपचारिक प्रतिपूर्ति (Reimbursement) मांगनी चाहिए।
विद्यालय के आधिकारिक खाते से आहरित एकाधिक उत्तर-दिनांकित (Post-dated) वाहक (Bearer) चेक जारी करके विक्रेता को दे देने चाहिए।
PFMS/NEFT/RTGS के माध्यम से विक्रेता के सत्यापित बैंक खाते में इलेक्ट्रॉनिक रूप से भुगतान करना चाहिए, क्योंकि नकद भुगतान पूर्णतः निषिद्ध है।

Issue multiple post-dated cash bearer cheques drawn on the school's official bank account.

questions.explanation_english: Under Rule 86 of GFR 2017 and the Central Government Account (Receipts and Payments) Rules, cash payments for commercial supplies, especially for substantial amounts like Rs. 40,000, are strictly illegal and prohibited. A Drawing and Disbursing Officer (DDO) or Principal must process all vendor payments electronically through PFMS, NEFT, or RTGS directly into the supplier's verified bank account. Using school revenue/fee collections directly to make disbursements is a serious financial irregularity violating GFR Rule 48 (which requires all revenues to be remitted intact into the government account). Paying via personal UPI accounts or issuing bearer cheques similarly circumvents statutory audit trails and violates government financial conduct. Hence, option D is the only legally valid course of action.
questions.explanation_hindi: GFR 2017 के नियम 86 तथा केंद्रीय सरकार लेखा (प्राप्ति एवं संदाय) नियमों के अनुसार, वाणिज्यिक आपूर्तिकर्ताओं को नकद में भुगतान करना, विशेष रूप से 40,000 रुपये जैसी बड़ी राशि के लिए, पूर्णतः वर्जित और गैर-कानूनी है। आहरण एवं संवितरण अधिकारी (DDO) या विद्यालय प्रमुख के रूप में प्राचार्य को विक्रेता के बिल का भुगतान केवल PFMS, NEFT या RTGS के माध्यम से सीधे विक्रेता के सत्यापित बैंक खाते में इलेक्ट्रॉनिक रूप से करना अनिवार्य है। विद्यालय में एकत्र दैनिक शुल्क या जुर्मानों से सीधे नकद भुगतान करना GFR नियम 48 (सभी प्राप्तियों को बिना किसी कटौती के सीधे सरकारी खाते में जमा करने का नियम) का खुला उल्लंघन है। व्यक्तिगत UPI से भुगतान करना अथवा वाहक चेक जारी करना भी गंभीर वित्तीय कदाचार माना जाता है। अतः विकल्प D सही उत्तर है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) Make payment electronically through PFMS/NEFT/RTGS to vendor's account, as cash payment is prohibited.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: PFMS/NEFT/RTGS to vendor's account, as cash payment is prohibited. Financial rules strictly prohibit making high- value commercial payments in physical cash. When settling vendor bills, institutional heads must execute payments electronically via PFMS, NEFT, or RTGS directly into the vendor's verified bank account. Cash payments or personal mobile applications bypass official banking trails and violate statutory financial processing guidelines.

options_hindi: व्यय प्रथम दृष्टया अवसर की मांग से अधिक नहीं होना चाहिए।
किसी प्राधिकारी को अपनी वित्तीय शक्तियों का प्रयोग स्वयं के लाभ के लिए नहीं करना चाहिए।
(A) और (B) दोनों।
न तो (A) और न ही (B); प्राचार्य को भत्तों की दरें बदलने का वैधानिक विवेकाधिकार प्राप्त है।

questions.question_english: A school Principal undertakes an official journey to attend a departmental meeting. Upon return, the Principal uses their delegated financial powers as Head of Office to sanction a Daily Allowance (DA) claim for themselves at a rate exceeding the statutory entitlement, arguing that the journey was exceptionally arduous. Which principle(s) of financial propriety under GFR 2017 has been violated?
options_english: Expenditure should not be prima facie more than the occasion demands.
No authority should exercise its powers of sanctioning expenditure to its own advantage.
Both (A) and (B).
Neither (A) nor (B); the Principal has statutory discretionary power to alter allowance rates.
questions.explanation_english:
The Principal has breached two fundamental canons of financial propriety codified in Rule 21 of GFR 2017:
1. Rule 21(ii) Violation: "The expenditure should not be prima facie more than the occasion demands." Sanctioning DA beyond the entitled limit constitutes an unjustified and inflated expense that is not warranted by statutory traveling allowance rules.
2. Rule 21(iv) Violation: "No authority should exercise its powers of sanctioning expenditure or to pass an order which will be directly or indirectly to its own advantage." A Drawing and Disbursing Officer cannot exercise delegated financial powers to grant themselves higher financial benefits or relax rules for their own enrichment. Any relaxation of TA/DA rules can only be considered by a competent superior authority (such as the Administrative Ministry/Department of Expenditure), never by the claimant officer.
questions.explanation_hindi:
प्राचार्य ने GFR 2017 के नियम 21 में संहिताबद्ध वित्तीय औचित्य के दो प्रमुख सिद्धांतों का उल्लंघन किया है:
1. नियम 21(ii) का उल्लंघन: "व्यय प्रथम दृष्टया अवसर की मांग से अधिक नहीं होना चाहिए।" निर्धारित हकदारी सीमा से अधिक दर पर दैनिक भत्ता स्वीकृत करना एक अनुचित और अत्यधिक व्यय है जो यात्रा भत्ता नियमों के अनुरूप नहीं है।
2. नियम 21(iv) का उल्लंघन: "किसी भी प्राधिकारी को व्यय स्वीकृत करने की अपनी शक्तियों का प्रयोग ऐसा आदेश पारित करने के लिए नहीं करना चाहिए जो प्रत्यक्ष या अप्रत्यक्ष रूप से उसके अपने लाभ के लिए हो।" कोई भी आहरण एवं संवितरण अधिकारी (DDO) स्वयं को वित्तीय लाभ पहुंचाने या नियमों में ढील देने के लिए अपनी शक्तियों का प्रयोग नहीं कर सकता। यात्रा भत्ता नियमों में किसी भी प्रकार की छूट केवल उच्च सक्षम प्राधिकारी (प्रशासनिक मंत्रालय/व्यय विभाग) द्वारा ही दी जा सकती है, स्वयं दावेदार द्वारा नहीं।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) Both (A) and (B).

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Sanctioning allowance rates exceeding statutory entitlements violates two fundamental standards of financial propriety. First, public expenditure must never exceed what the occasion legitimately requires under established rules. Second, an administrative authority cannot exercise financial power to bestow monetary advantages upon itself. Deviating from prescribed travel allowance caps for personal financial benefit represents a direct breach of both core propriety principles.

questions.question_hindi: एक सरकारी विद्यालय का शिक्षक जो आधिकारिक चुनाव ड्यूटी पर जा रहा है, यात्रा भत्ता (टीए) अग्रिम का अनुरोध करता है। ड्यूटी से लौटने के बाद, शिक्षक छह महीने तक टीए समायोजन बिल प्रस्तुत करने में विफल रहता है। वित्तीय नियमों के अनुसार कार्यालय प्रमुख / प्राचार्य को क्या कार्रवाई करनी चाहिए?
options_hindi: पिछली बकाया राशि को स्वतः समाहित करने के लिए अगले दौरे हेतु एक और नया टीए अग्रिम प्रदान करना।
चुनाव ड्यूटी के महत्व को ध्यान में रखते हुए प्रशासनिक देरी को पूरी तरह से माफ कर देना।
दंडात्मक ब्याज सहित शिक्षक के वेतन से पूरे बकाया टीए अग्रिम की एकमुश्त वसूली करना।
कार्यालय प्रमुख के विशेष अनुमोदन से असमायोजित अग्रिम को अधिकृत अनुग्रह भुगतान (ex-gratia) में परिवर्तित करना।

questions.question_english: A government school teacher going on an official election duty tour requests a Travelling Allowance (TA) advance. Upon returning from the tour, the teacher fails to submit the TA adjustment bill for six months. What action should the Head of Office / Principal take as per financial rules?
options_english: Grant another fresh TA advance for the next duty to automatically absorb the previous outstanding balance.
Condone the administrative delay entirely considering that the tour was conducted for official election duty.
Recover the entire outstanding TA advance from the teacher's salary in a lump sum along with penal interest.
Convert the unadjusted advance into an authorized ex-gratia payment with special approval from the Head of Office.
questions.explanation_english:
Under Supplementary Rules (SR) and the Compendium of Rules on Advances:
1. Statutory Time Limit: A government servant who draws a TA advance on tour is required to submit the final adjustment travel claim within 15 days of completing the return journey.
2. Mandatory Recovery: When an employee fails to submit the adjustment bill within the prescribed statutory period, the administrative head / DDO must enforce mandatory financial recovery. The entire outstanding advance amount must be recovered in a single lump sum from the employee's subsequent monthly salary disbursement.
3. Penal Interest: In addition to lump-sum recovery, penal interest (at 2% above the prevailing GPF interest rate) is charged on the unadjusted advance from the date of drawal to the date of recovery.
4. No Discretion: The Head of Office has no administrative power to condone the delay arbitrarily, write off the advance, convert it into an ex-gratia grant, or issue a second advance before the first is settled.
Therefore, the correct action is to recover the entire advance from the salary in a lump sum.
questions.explanation_hindi:
पूरक नियमों (SR) और अग्रिम नियमों के संग्रह के अनुसार:
1. वैधानिक समय-सीमा: आधिकारिक दौरे पर टीए अग्रिम लेने वाले सरकारी सेवक को वापसी यात्रा पूरी होने के 15 दिनों के भीतर अंतिम यात्रा समायोजन बिल प्रस्तुत करना अनिवार्य होता है।
2. अनिवार्य वसूली: जब कोई कर्मचारी निर्धारित समय-सीमा के भीतर यात्रा भत्ता समायोजन बिल प्रस्तुत करने में विफल रहता है, तो प्रशासनिक प्रमुख / डीडीओ को अनिवार्य वित्तीय वसूली करनी होती है। पूरी बकाया अग्रिम राशि कर्मचारी के आगामी वेतन से एकमुश्त वसूल की जानी चाहिए।
3. दंडात्मक ब्याज: एकमुश्त वसूली के अलावा, आहरण की तारीख से वसूली की तारीख तक असमायोजित अग्रिम पर दंडात्मक ब्याज (GPF दर से 2% अधिक) भी लगाया जाता है।
4. कोई विवेकाधिकार नहीं: कार्यालय प्रमुख के पास मनमाने ढंग से देरी को माफ करने, इसे बट्टे खाते में डालने, इसे अनुग्रह अनुदान (ex-gratia) में बदलने या पिछला अग्रिम चुकता किए बिना दूसरा अग्रिम जारी करने का कोई अधिकार नहीं है।
अतः सही कार्रवाई शिक्षक के वेतन से पूरी बकाया राशि की एकमुश्त वसूली करना है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) Recover the entire outstanding TA advance from the teacher's salary in a lump sum.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: from the teacher's salary in a lump sum. When an employee fails to submit a travel allowance adjustment bill within the stipulated statutory period following tour completion, the administrative head must enforce financial recovery. The entire outstanding advance amount must be recovered in a single lump sum from the employee's subsequent salary payment, alongside penal interest if mandated under financial rules.

questions.question_hindi: एक अनुबंधित विक्रेता किसी उचित कारण के बिना निर्धारित संविदात्मक समय-सीमा के भीतर एक सरकारी विद्यालय में फर्नीचर की आपूर्ति करने में विफल रहता है। आपूर्ति में हुई इस देरी के लिए पूर्व-आकलित क्षति की वसूली हेतु प्राचार्य/आहरण एवं संवितरण अधिकारी (DDO) को किस अनुबंधात्मक प्रावधान को लागू करना चाहिए?

questions.question_english: A contracted vendor fails to deliver classroom furniture to a government school within the stipulated contractual delivery period without any justifiable reason. Which contractual remedy should the Principal/DDO enforce to recover pre-estimated damages for the delay?
options_english: Force Majeure clause
Liquidated Damages (LD) clause
Price Variation Clause (PVC)
Mandatory Arbitration clause
questions.explanation_english: Under Rule 225 of GFR 2017 and the Manual for Procurement of Goods issued by the Ministry of Finance, public contracts must contain a Liquidated Damages (LD) clause to protect the Government from unexcused delivery delays. When a supplier fails to deliver goods or complete services within the agreed delivery schedule and an extension is granted without waiving damages, the competent authority/Principal is required to levy and deduct Liquidated Damages from the contractor's bills. LD represents a genuine pre-estimate of damages suffered due to delay, standardly calculated at a fixed percentage (commonly 0.5% of the price of delayed stores per week of delay or part thereof), subject to a prescribed maximum ceiling (usually 10% of the total contract value). Hence, option B is correct.
questions.explanation_hindi: GFR 2017 के नियम 225 और वित्त मंत्रालय के वस्तु खरीद मैनुअल के अनुसार, सरकारी अनुबंधों में आपूर्ति में अनुचित देरी से निपटने के लिए परिनिर्धारित हर्जाना खंड (Liquidated Damages - LD Clause) शामिल किया जाना अनिवार्य है। जब कोई ठेकेदार या विक्रेता बिना किसी वैध कारण (जैसे फोर्स मेज्योर) के तय समय-सीमा के भीतर सामग्री (जैसे विद्यालय फर्नीचर) की आपूर्ति करने में विफल रहता है, तो प्राचार्य/DDO को विक्रेता के बिलों से लिक्विडेटेड डैमेज (LD) की कटौती करनी होती है। यह राशि प्रशासनिक व संस्थागत असुविधा और देरी से हुई क्षति का पूर्व-निर्धारित वास्तविक आकलन होती है, जो सामान्यतः प्रति सप्ताह 0.5% की दर से अधिकतम 10% तक काटी जाती है। अतः विकल्प B सही उत्तर है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Liquidated Damages (LD) clause

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: When a supplier or contractor fails to deliver goods or complete services within the stipulated contractual delivery timeframe, the buyer enforces the Liquidated Damages clause. This contractual remedy allows deducting pre-estimated, agreed damages--typically calculated as a specified percentage per week of delay--from vendor bills to compensate for administrative delays.

questions.question_english:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): Fixed assets must be recorded in the government asset register at their original historical cost (purchase price).
Reason (R): GFR 2017 requires that the recorded value of fixed assets in the register be updated annually to reflect prevailing market inflation rates.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options_english: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is true but (R) is false
(A) is false but (R) is true
questions.explanation_english:
Under Form GFR-22 and Rule 211 of GFR 2017:
- Assertion (A) is true: Fixed assets and non-consumable stores must be recorded in Form GFR-22 at their original historical acquisition cost (which includes invoice price, statutory duties/taxes, freight, handling, and initial installation or commissioning charges).
- Reason (R) is false: Government accounting operates on the principle of historical cost accounting. GFR does not provide for or permit annual revaluation or upward indexation of asset register values based on fluctuating market inflation rates. The historical cost remains the benchmark until the asset is condemned and disposed of or depreciated where commercial/accrual accounting standards apply.
Therefore, (A) is true, but (R) is false.
questions.explanation_hindi:

questions.question_english: Which of the following statements correctly identifies the regulatory nature of advances granted to government employees for official tours and departmental transfers?
options_english: They carry a heavy compound interest rate equivalent to General Provident Fund (GPF) rates.
They are non-interest-bearing advances meant to meet contingent duty and travel expenses.
They are permanent non-recoverable monetary grants that do not require formal submission of adjustment bills.
They can be sanctioned exclusively by the Department of Expenditure under the Ministry of Finance.
questions.explanation_english:
Under GFR and Supplementary Rules (SR) governing Travelling Allowances, advances sanctioned to government employees for official tours and departmental transfers are strictly non-interest-bearing financial accommodations. The rationale is that an employee proceeding on official duty should not be forced to incur out-of-pocket personal expenditure for public service.
Key regulatory provisions:
1. Tour and transfer advances are provided to meet immediate travel and contingent expenses incurred while performing official duties.
2. Employees are strictly required to settle these advances by submitting detailed adjustment bills accompanied by supporting travel vouchers within prescribed statutory timeframes (15 days for tour TA).
3. If an employee fails to submit adjustment bills in time, penal interest is levied and the unadjusted amount is recovered in a lump sum from the salary.
4. Powers to sanction these routine duty advances are delegated to Heads of Offices and DDOs under the Delegation of Financial Powers Rules (DFPR).
